PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 1.
FADE IN:
TIGHT ON - A giggling BABY EMERSON, bouncing up and down.
Emerson Cod was 5 months, 3 days and 4 hours
old when his mother planned his death.
FIND - CALISTA COD, COOING and playing “airplane” with her baby
at the top of the courthouse steps. She settles the tot back
into his pram, then shoves it down the stone staircase.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
It would be quick, painless...
Calista SCREAMS! PASSERSBY dive for the pram as it bounces down
the stairs and smashes into a mailbox. The baby goes hurtling,
but is suddenly plucked from the air by DENNIS DALWHIMPLE, whose
smile drops when he realizes he’s holding -- A BABY DOLL.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and the easiest way for Private Detective
Calista Cod to bust Dennis Dalwhimple, a stock
clerk claiming millions in pain and suffering as
the result of a forklift accident.
POP WIDE - Dennis, in leg casts and a back brace, has jumped out
of his wheelchair to make the catch. A CAMERA FLASHES.
Calista steps in to grab another shot. Her trench coat falls
open, revealing Baby Emerson, safely strapped to her in a
papoose. Mother and son glare at the criminal before them.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
While most children with single, working
mothers were banished to mundane day care
centers, Emerson Cod -- code name: “Lil’
GumShoe” -- reveled in on-the-job training as
his mother’s best friend and business partner.

scenes.heading: INT. CALISTA’S OFFICE (ONE WALL) - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Calista and a husky YOUNG EMERSON sit behind a desk with “MS.
COD” and “MR. COD” nameplates. A brave-faced WIFE is across
from them. She offers up a PHOTO of her HUSBAND.
The firm of Cod & Cod dedicated itself to the
pursuit of truth at all costs...
CAMERA ZOOMS IN on the HUSBAND’S PHOTO. PULL BACK TO FIND...
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
Young Emerson waits as Calista ties a rope around his ankles.
...a pursuit Young Emerson found “badass.”
The HUSBAND from the photo kisses his MISTRESS as, OUTSIDE THE
WINDOW... a gleeful Young Emerson drops UPSIDE DOWN INTO FRAME.
Faced with scoundrels, cheats and the havoc they
wreaked, mother and son made a vow: to never let
lies come between them.
A FLASH from Emerson’s CAMERA takes us back to--

scenes.heading: INT. CALISTA’S OFFICE (ONE WALL) - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: The now teary-eyed wife studies the PHOTO. She hands over a
STACK OF CASH and exits. Calista splits the money with Emerson.
It was a profitable decision. For as the
Cods’ bond grew, so did business, and cemented
in the detectives’ hearts that truth is the
cornerstone of any successful relationship.
An ILLUSTRATION of a PIGTAILED GIRL, hanging upside down by a
rope and peeking into a motel window, FILLS FRAME.
Years later, as in now, Private Investigator
Emerson Cod found himself less successful in
another venture: aspiring pop-up book author.
The illustrated rope MOVES, hoisting the girl back up. FIND -
ADULT EMERSON, pulling a tab of his POP-UP BOOK, “Lil’ GumShoe.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
“Lil’ GumShoe” was based on the detective’s exciting
childhood adventures. However, its greater purpose
was for his missing daughter who, as a baby, had
been spirited away by his ruthless ex. The P.I.
hoped that the child would find hidden in the story
the map that could lead her back to him. If only it
had not been rejected by every pop-up publisher.
Emerson pores over a stack of rejection letters.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED:
“Complex plot, lack of theme, child
endangerment.” Man, that’s cold.
So, at this moment, Emerson Cod, a failure at
fatherhood and fiction, decided to quit.
As Emerson sets fire to one of the letters with his cigar...

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - NIGHT

lines.text: ...A FLAME touches the end of a cigarillo.
NED (O.S.)
Who is she?
CHUCK (O.S.)
Don’t know. She just rolled in. Like a
moody, mean thundercloud.
NED and CHUCK steal glances at a BROAD in her 60s, smoking a
cigarillo. She BANGS her glass. OLIVE approaches, re-fills it.
Know what you want?
Yeah. Nothin’, with a side of buzz off.
She goes back to her newspaper. Ned steps up.
Ma’am, sorry to bother, but perhaps you didn’t
realize this is an eating establishment and not a
park bench, for example, where one can loiter and
smoke and not consume food to one’s heart’s content.
Got a problem, we can take it outside.
Ned and Olive retreat back to Chuck.
Maybe I can get her to ask me to take it
outside. Then, I’ll say, “Okay. After you.”
Then, when she goes, I’ll slam the door and
lock it behind her.
A dejected Emerson enters.
Ooh, good! Someone with a gun.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.
CONTINUED:
Rhubarb. Whole pie’ll do.
(stops, smells something)
And, Momma, when will you treat yourself right
and spring for a decent stogie?
The next time I trail a white-collar money
launderer to Havana.
He wraps her in a hug as the Pie Holers stand by, speechless.
People, meet the P.I. who taught me everything
I know. Also happens to be my best bud and
momma to boot -- Calista Cod.
I’m Ned. This is Chuck and Olive. Sorry, we
didn’t know. Although, we should’ve. I mean,
in retrospect, it makes a lot of sense
actually.
So, Calista, what brings you to our neck of
the woods?
A fraud case. And, I’ve been missin’ my Lil’
GumShoe.
(to Emerson)
Now, can we hit a bar? I’m starving.
OMIT
Chuck joins Ned, who is tidying up for the night.
Wasn’t she comforting? The brutal honesty, the
sardonic wit, the appetite for hooch. Add an
eyepatch, and Calista could be Lily.
How are you doing with that?
What’s “that”?
Living with the fact that the woman you’ve
known your whole life as a tied-for-first-
place favorite aunt is really your mother.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED:
Oh, that “that.” Well, I’m happy to have a
mother who’s alive. I’m not as happy she can’t
know I’m alive. Oh, no. Suddenly, what I found
comforting before is giving way to sadness.
Then I’ll be your comforter. Consider me a
king-sized duvet ready to wrap you in goose-
down goodness. Tonight.
I’d love to, but I have plans with Olive.
You two have hung out every night since she
got back. Not that I’m counting. Are you
like new best friends or something?
No. Wait. Why not? I mean, I guess she is.
I have a new best friend. Isn’t that superb?
The Pie-Maker did not think so, for the more
time Chuck spent with her new best friend, the
less time she had for him. He felt alone.
But he feared the truth would make him sound
needy, so instead, he lied.
It sure is. Superb. For you. Both.
Olive enters from the dining room. To Chuck:
Wanna head home, roomie?
Charlotte Charles and Olive Snook’s decision
to cohabitate was sudden, just like Olive’s
earlier decision to join a nunnery...

scenes.heading: EXT. NUNNERY - COURTYARD - DAY - FLASHBACK (EP 201/SC 43 RE-USE)

lines.text: Olive’s face drops as DOZENS OF POOR bumrush her belongings.
...where all her earthly possessions had been
given to the poor. It was a gesture she’d all
but forgotten until she arrived home with a
new pet pig by her side...
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.

scenes.heading: INT. OLIVE AND CHUCK’S APARTMENT - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Accompanied by PIGBY, Olive enters, finds Chuck packing.
...and found Charlotte Charles and all her
earthly possessions residing there.
I’m moving out. Having moved in, which
organically came out of missing you. And
watering your plants. Like you asked. Don’t
worry. Tomorrow, this’ll all be gone.
Olive notices DIGBY asleep in a corner. Pigby sniffs him.
Everything? Even the couch, the curtains, that
adorable ceramic cheese set?
I figured you’d want to start from scratch.
Truthfully, Olive Snook did not. What she
wanted was a furnished apartment, so she
gambled on her squatter’s accommodating nature
and said:
Scratch that. Let’s be roommates!
No, I couldn’t impose.
Truthfully, Charlotte Charles could. Like
Olive Snook, she enjoyed her things and the
feeling of independence they brought her, so
she gambled on her quasi-landlady’s
accommodating nature and said:
But if I were to impose, you should know I’m
a morning showerer, a heavy sleeper and a
dish drier.
I’m a late-night bath taker, a snorer and a
dish scrubber. Welcome home!
Is there anything bigger we should discuss?
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED:
If you’re referring to the time you made me
an unwitting drug mule for your aunts...
Oh. I wasn’t, but--
Good! ‘Cause I done roasted that old chestnut.
And I’m fine with how you hid the fact that one
of those aunts was really my mother.
Right... Just like I’m a-okay with you not
explaining to me why you faked your own death.
My, look at all those bridges--
And all that water flowing under them. I’m
proud of us. For having the courage put it
all on the table, deal with the tough stuff--
And then quickly move off it.
Chuck and Olive had simultaneous and sneaking
suspicions that they were fooling themselves.
But they read each other’s anxiety as giddy
excitement, so Olive Snook changed the subject
with the help of two four-legged creatures.
‘Sides, who woulda’ thought they’d hit it off?
She indicates Digby and Pigby, now napping together.
Which reminds me, mind if I take the bed by
the window?
Absolutely... not!
OFF Olive, pretending not to mind at all...
OMIT
TIGHT ON - Emerson, clearly uncomfortable as Calista helps him
squeeze into a knitted double-shoulder holster.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED:
Knew I should’ve knitted it larger.
Wool stretches.
Not to China, sweetheart. Hey. You got a
girl somewhere?
Emerson freezes at the sight of his mother, perched on the desk
next to -- the pop-up book and the rejection letters.
Emerson Cod had lied to his best friend and
mother about two things. One: that he did have
a girl somewhere, age 7. Two: that he had
written a book designed to bring this girl back
into his life. The guilt he felt over these
secrets was immense, and the primary reason he
had begun to limit his contact with Calista.
Girl? Why?
Someone’s been feeding you. What’s her name?
Pie-Maker.
Damn. And damn sad, me not knowin’ what’s
happening in your life. I know we’re both
busy, but it’s not right.
Emerson Cod agreed. It was no longer right to be
in his mother’s presence without coming clean and
cleaning off their cornerstone. His decision to
share his secrets was a noble intent...
Here’s the dilly, Ma--
...if not for another visitor.
At that moment, a FEMALE SILHOUETTE appears at the office door.
VERONICA VILLANUEVA -- busty, sexy -- enters.
Mr. Cod, I’m in desperate need of assistance.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
CONTINUED: (2)
What has you so desperate, Miss...?
Villanueva. Veronica Villanueva. An unsolved
murder. Namely, that of my best friend, Joe.
Office is closed. Family matters.
Please. I’m opening my heart to you.
Just open that blouse.
Veronica does, to REVEAL a wad of cash. Calista takes it, not
noticing Emerson’s dismay. He locks the book and rejection
letters in a filing cabinet and turns back to Veronica.
Got a description of this Joe?
Picture’s worth a thousand words.
She pulls a STACK OF PHOTOS from her blouse, hands them over.
CLOSE ON - THE PHOTOGRAPHS - Veronica and a handsome man, JOE,
get mani-pedis, drink cosmos, shop, do yoga.
VERONICA (CONT’D)
They found his body dumped in an alley last
night. He’d been missing for two days.
Cops got anything?
They shut me out for not being family. But
Joe was like a brother. He meant everything
to me. I want justice at any price.
That’s our kinda’ justice. We’ll be in touch.
Veronica exits.
I’ll be dental damned.
With a girl like that, you certainly should.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED: (3)
Talkin’ ‘bout a dentist by the name of Dr.
Eugene Halifax. Came in this morning about
the murder of his best friend, Joe.
Emerson unearths another set of photos. They depict the same
Joe with DR. EUGENE HALIFAX (short, bookish, balding) as they
rock climb, skydive, guzzle beer and floss.
(off Veronica’s photos)
With Miss Villanueva, he’s a cosmo-drinkin’
shopaholic. Queer.
You bet it’s odd. Dr. Eugene’s got him as a
tough guy who’s tough on plaque. Seems Joe
was a different friend to different people.
Meaning both your clients. Gonna thank Momma
for getting you paid twice to solve one murder?
A SHEET FLIPS UP, pulled back by Emerson. He, Ned and Chuck
stare at JOE’S BODY.
That’s Joe, all right.
Ned sets his watch, reaches out and SPARK! Joe opens his eyes.
They glint like an Up with People rally.
Heya, folks. What’s goin’ on?
You’re in the county morgue. Our condolences.
Happen to know how you happened in here?
Last I remember, I was getting ready to play
ball when suddenly, there was a doozy of a pain
in my back.
There’s a crudely sewn-up wound on Joe’s upper back/shoulder.
Stab wound. Killer stitched it up. Poorly.
Lemme see.
He sits up. WHOOSH! Clear fluid rushes from the wound.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED:
JOE (CONT’D)
What the hay?
Joe BLOCKS the flow with his hand, causing fluid to SPURT from
his ear, instead. Chuck PLUGS his ear with her finger.
JOE (CONT’D)
Thank you.
You’re welcome. Is it just me, or is that
odor reminiscent of 8th-grade Biology.
Specifically, formaldehyde.
The coroner must’ve already embalmed me.
Coroner don’t embalm. Just looks for cause of
death. Preservin’ happens after ‘n’ elsewhere.
Joe covers his mouth, SNEEZES. Liquid SHOOTS across the room.
Bless you.
No, bless Downy. She was my one and only.
Never gotta chance to tell her how much I
cared. Now, she’ll never know.
Any thoughts as to who might’ve wanted to
pickle your gherkin?
None. Honestly, I’ve always considered myself
pretty darn affable. Huh. Wonder if it has
something to do with my best friend?
Which one? Veronica or Dr. Eugene?
You know those two? Small world! Such a cold
one, too. I don’t know what they’ll do without
me. Promise you’ll keep an eye on ‘em?
Oh, we aim to.
Ned touches Joe. FLASH! He falls back onto the table.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 12.
CONTINUED: (2)
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Looks like we gotta get more friendly with a
coupla’ best friends.
There’s an O.S. TRICKLE of liquid from the morgue table.
And a mop.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 13.
FADE IN:
Emerson and Calista stand across from Veronica and DR. EUGENE.
Under normal circumstances, a P.I. would
question separate clients separately. However,
the presence of one P.I.’s P.I. mother allowed
him to employ a time-saving interrogation
technique known as the Kalashni-Cod. Like the
Russian machine gun for which it was named, its
operation was simple. The scope was set...
Emerson levels his gaze on Eugene. Calista takes Veronica. The
P.I.s SLAM their hands, in unison, on the desk.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...the magazine loaded and the trigger pulled.
Who’s Joe’s best friend? Who’s Joe’s best friend?
Both suspects raise their hand.
Got it on good authority Joe’s BFF made him
RIP. Who wants the title now?
Veronica and Eugene point at one another.
EMERSON (CONT’D) CALISTA
Where were you last Friday Where were you last Friday
night, pearly? night, girly?
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Were you obsessed?
Where’d you buy the formaldehyde?
Did givin’ him the stab-stab feel good?
What is this? I’m not a suspect. I hired you.
...And I think I’d like my money back.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 14.
CONTINUED:
I don’t give refunds to people who waste my
time. When my services are retained, I
require the facts. All of ‘em. But lookin’
at you two -- the averted eyes...
...the lowered heads...
...the nibbled lips -- tells me you’re hiding
something.
SLAMMING their hands in unison again--
EMERSON (CONT’D) CALISTA
What is it? What is it?
Fine. Here’s the truth. The dirty,
humiliating truth. Joe was a Frescort.
It’s short for “friend-escort.” Basically, a
friend for hire. You pick from a catalogue,
and they become anyone you want them to be.
What’s wrong with pickin’ someone the old-
fashioned way? Walking up and sayin’, “Hi,
I’m Blah-dee-blah. You like bloo-dee-blooin’?
Me, too. Let’s be friends.”
But I’m shy. When I try that, I start
sweating, my brain goes numb and I suffer
awful xerostomia. Cottonmouth.
Emerson pulls out the pictures of Joe and Eugene.
You tellin’ me you had the guts to jump out of
a plane, but not into a happy hour?
I thought all those stunts would help build my
confidence. They didn’t.
(to Veronica)
I get why Dr. Bashful needs a pay-a-pal.
But back when I had a rack and coupla’
getaway sticks like yours, I had no problem
makin’ acquaintances.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 15.
CONTINUED: (2)
Initial contact is easy. This...
(gesturing to her body)
...attracts all kinds. But no one wants to
get to know who I am. Men only see me as a
score not-yet-scored.
And the women?
(off her body again)
This...
Yeah, we got it.
...prompts instant jealousy. I was all alone.
Yearning for genuine companionship. So, I
called in the professionals.
She offers a business card, which reads: “MY BEST FRIEND, INC.”
As Emerson Cod read the words, he was reminded
of Frescort Joe’s final ones. That his murder
may have had to do with:
My Best Friend. Inc.

scenes.heading: EXT. MY BEST FRIEND, INC. - DAY

lines.text: A BUBBLE-LETTER SIGN reads: “MY BEST FRIEND, INC.” PAN TO FIND --
EMERSON’S CAR, parked across the street.
Emerson scopes the building with Ned, Chuck and Olive.
Everyone clear on their role in this?
Olive and I are Frescort wannabes. Our
mission: to find Joe’s “one and only” Downy.
Who can hopefully tell us why Joe is now
Frescorting at that big mixer in the sky.
Meantime, me and the pie-man’ll have a sit-
down chitty-chat with the CEO.
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 16.
CONTINUED:
Find out who Joe was pretend-friending the
night he died. Any questions?
Ned raises his hand.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
That there was rhetorical.
My query is not. What happened to you and
your mom working this together?
She’s workin’ her own case, and I might need a
diversion, so, as I said, you’re with me.
(raising his hand)
This isn’t a question. More of a suggestion.
Merely a tiny change of plan where Chuck goes
undercover with... me, for instance.
The Pie-Maker’s intention wasn’t to make waves.
He was just trying to spend time with his beloved
and always-otherwise-occupied-lately Chuck.
Sure. It’s just, Olive and I kind of already
came up with aliases and back-stories--
And a secret incognito-partners’ handshake.
Which Chuck and Olive demonstrate.
Nice. Plan stays as planned. Move out.

scenes.heading: INT. MY BEST FRIEND, INC. - BUDDY’S OFFICE - DAY

lines.text: CLOSE ON - A NAME TAG: “BUDDY AMICUS, CEO.”
BUDDY (O.S.)
Welcome to My Best Friend! Where everyone’s
in the in-crowd.
REVEAL BUDDY, handsome and warm. Arms outstretched, he steps
toward Ned and Emerson. They take a simultaneous step back.
I’m a P.I. Less interested in the in-crowd
and more in the out. As in, murdered.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 17.
CONTINUED:
You’re here about Joe. Such a devastating
loss. He was our top performer.
That what you peddle? “Performers”?
Truthfully? I’d say it’s atonement.
Buddy gestures to his office full of high school memorabilia:
pennants, trophies, etc. Sporting equipment lines the walls.
BUDDY (CONT’D)
Back in high school, I was a colossal creep.
Math geeks, male cheerleaders, even our
pitiful team mascot, were just sad, pimply
targets for a varsity quarterback like me.
Buddy eyes a QUARTERBACK MANNEQUIN, housed in a glass case.
BUDDY (CONT’D)
Until two blitzing linebackers destroyed my
knee and put me on the DL the rest of the
season. Suddenly, I was no different from
all those nerds I put through hell. From
that point on, I swore I’d use my powers for
good, providing -- at a nominal fee -- what
everyone has the right to: friendship.
From the looks of these digs, your nominal
fees are addin’ up.
No matter how much the modern world thinks
gadgetry has brought us together, it’s driven
us further apart. We converse via electrical
wires, hide behind glowing screens and then,
after weeks become years, finally look up to
discover we no longer know what personal
connection is or even how to make one. We’re
isolated. All alone. And being alone is hard.
Yes. I mean, certainly. It can be.
Here at My Best Friend, Inc., we strive to
fill that chasm of loneliness. Once trained,
my Frescorts integrate seamlessly into
clients’ lives and function as the best
companions money can buy.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
CONTINUED: (2)
Who was Joe companioning the night he died?
Let me check his file.
Buddy rifles through a stack of files on his desk, opens one
marked: “JOE.”
BUDDY (CONT’D)
No client appointments.
Mind if I take a gander?
We keep all records confidential.
Buddy notices Ned looking at a two-armed contraption.
BUDDY (CONT’D)
Ah. The Hug Machine. Our most valuable
teaching tool.
How ‘bout a demonstration on my associate?
No, thank you.
(low)
Divert.
Come on, you! See, proper hugs are a science.
Buddy puts Ned into the machine, flips a switch. The metal arms
close. Meanwhile, Emerson scans Joe’s unattended file.
BUDDY (CONT’D)
They must be platonic, but not cold. Firm but
not painful...
The Pie-Maker didn’t want to be hugged by a
machine. He wanted to be hugged by the one he was
lonely for. But to his surprise, Buddy Amicus was
right. Proper hugs were a science. As the clinch
grew stronger, so did the warm and satisfying
feeling inside him. For a fleeting moment, the
Pie-Maker’s aloneness abated. So he closed his
eyes, thought of Chuck and hugged back.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 19.
CONTINUED: (3)
I like that.
We’ll have models in the gift shop by Christmas.
I’ll stick one in your stocking. Let’s go.
Emerson Cod had uncovered Joe’s home address...

scenes.heading: INT. MY BEST FRIEND, INC. - LOBBY - DAY

lines.text: Chuck and Olive enter a lobby bustling with CLIENTS.
...as Chuck and Olive addressed going undercover.
The girls approach a welcome desk shaped like an Irish
friendship ring. It’s manned by BARB, a bubbly Frescort.
Are you Barb? I’m Kitty Pimms. This is Patty
Boots. We’re two highly-motivated candidates
here to befriend the sad and lonely.
For pay.
You already passed the first test.
(singsong)
“Kitty Pimms, Patty Boots, Kitty-Kitty-Kitty,
Patty.” What wonderfully rhythmic names.
They just scream “good humor” and “bonhomie.”
Now. Can you “F-f-fake It Real”?
W-w-what?
Were you making fun of my stuttering?
No, I was just--
Passing the second test. See, I don’t stutter,
but if I did, what you just did would put me at
ease by subtly saying, “You’re OK; I’m OK;
We’re OK, OK?” That’s what’s so wonderful
about this job. We get to help people feel
comfortable. Kitty, we’re at a dinner party.
There’s spinach stuck in my teeth. Whadya do?
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 20.
CONTINUED:
Stick an even bigger piece in mine?
“B” to the “I” to the “N-G-O.” Now, back to “F-
f-fake It Real,” which isn’t about stuttering
but copyright infringement. An erotic toy
company nabbed “Fake It Real” before us, but no
matter what you call it, it’s our key to
successful Frescorting. On any given day,
clients are going to depend on you to summon up
every feeling in the book, even if you’re not
feeling it. Show me “happy.”
Chuck and Olive smile, then change their looks to comply with:
BARB (CONT’D)
“Sad,” “surprise,” “fear,” “zest,” “consternation,”
“constipation.” Know what I’m showing you? “Heck,
yeah!” We’re getting you into training ASAP.
Is a course in self-defense included? I hear
this job can be dangerous.
You’re referring to Joe. So horrible.
Did you know him?
Just by name. Frescorts are forbidden to
fraternize. We focus all our energies on
clients, not each other. You two are friends,
aren’t you? Don’t answer, I can tell. Thing
is, you’re awesome, and I only want to bring
the best people into this organization, so
keep things on the q.t.
We won’t even carpool.
At that moment, another carpool had landed at
the apartment of a murder victim.

scenes.heading: INT. APARTMENT HALLWAY - JOE’S DOOR - DAY

lines.text: Emerson and Ned move down the hall.
Somethin’ off about Frescortville. People
come in hungry for connection, and they’re
served up a smörgåsbord o’ lies.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 21.
CONTINUED:
They arrive at a door. Emerson gets to picking the lock.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Those Frescorts are cons hiding behind good
intentions. My experience: people don’t
appreciate being conned, even if they’re
pathetic losers who signed up for it in the
first place. Now, we’re gonna find Joe’s list
of clients. Find out if one ‘em did him in.
Why are they pathetic losers? ‘Cause they’re alone?
‘Cause they’re payin’ for something that’s free.
There’s nothing wrong with needing a little extra
help. No one thinks twice if a person with a
wobbly backhand hires a tennis coach. And I’m
guessing you have no clue how to bake a rhubarb
custard pie. But do I call you pathetic for
paying me to do it? You’ve had a best friend
since birth. Not all of us are that lucky.
Don’t be jealous of my luck. Ain’t nothing
but one sorry leaf hanging off that clover.
(a beat)
Momma and me aren’t supposed to have any lies
between us. Now, technically, I never lied.
But I also never told her I have a daughter.
Most mothers would consider that splitting hairs.
She spent her whole life teachin’ me how to
collar cons. Guess I’m embarrassed havin’ her
know my baby’s mother conned me. But I’m
chucking my chagrin overboard, lettin’ loose
the truth. Yep. Gonna sit her down, take a
deep breath and look her straight in the--
Hi!
The door has opened to REVEAL RANDY MANN. He holds a set of
giant tweezers, which grip a glass eye. And OFF this...
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 22.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: INT. APARTMENT HALLWAY - JOE’S DOOR - DAY

lines.text: The goofy-yet-gregarious Randy smiles at Ned and Emerson, who
can’t look away from the eye in Randy’s grip.
Uh-oh. Cat got your eye? Priceless! Sorry.
This bothering you? It’s just glass. For a
sculpture I’m working on. Gonna be a beaut.
Mind stowin’ it for a bit? We’re
investigators, here about a murder.
Randy ushers them into the tidy apartment.
Joe was my roommate.
And what’s your name, roommate?
Randy Mann. I’ve got some knee-slappers about
that. Wanna hear? Probably not. In the face
of tragedy, I try to keep things light. It’s
just weird, not having him here anymore. Joe
had such a big personality.
The Pie-Maker identified with the affable
Randy Mann, for he, too, was struggling to
stay positive in the face of his own tragedy.
It’s tough. You share your life with someone,
then suddenly, there’s an abyss where a person
always was before.
You lost a roommate, too?
And girlfriend. Same person.
Dude, your roommate-slash-girlfriend died?
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 23.
CONTINUED:
Yeah. I mean, no. She moved out. Sorry.
Doesn’t compare. Not even remotely.
Oblivious, Randy plucks a hair from Ned’s jacket, inspects it.
But you’re not completely alone. Golden
retriever, right?
Yes. Digby. Who’d be a source of comfort if
he didn’t prefer bunking with my girlfriend,
her new bestie and their pig.
Emerson shoots daggers at Ned.
You aware Joe worked as a friend for hire, Mann?
I thought he was a tutor for “special folks”
or something like that.
Happen to know who he was with the night he died?
Sure don’t, pal. What are you doing?
Emerson heads for a back room.
Bedrooms back here? I wanna see Joe’s.
For a moment, Randy’s mood darkens as he blocks Emerson’s path
and shuts the door.
Wish you could, but ya can’t. I’m late for
something. Seriously, though, come back anytime.
OFF his winning smile...
Emerson and Calista sit with Ned, Chuck and Olive.
Randy’s a nutjob’s name.
Totally. If one Randy isn’t tossing small
animals off bridges--
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 24.
CONTINUED:
Another’s luring small children under them.
Chuck and Olive had decided to test their
Frescort skills and fake a real connection
with one tough customer, Calista Cod.
These gals know what I’m talkin’ about.
Randy can also be a fun guy’s name. You grab
a beer with Randy. Grill brats with Randy.
Pick up chicks with Randy--
And help stuff ‘em in Randy’s freezer with Randy.
Can you be a little nice? His roommate died.
Notice how nice ‘n’ crazy-behind-the-eyes he
got when I tried to get into that back room?
What’s he hidin’ in there?
People are private. I’ve never seen your
back room.
I’ve never seen your front room.
I’ve never seen your front door. Where do you
live, anyway?
(to Calista)
Your son is rather secretive.
He didn’t get it from me.
My hizzy ain’t none of ya’ll’s bizzy. Randy
Mann’s shady. I’m getting back in his place.
Just gotta wait for him to take my bait.
(to Chuck and Olive)
Meantime, what’ve you got?
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 25.
CONTINUED: (2)
No sign of Downy yet. And since company
policy dictates Frescorts can’t date, it might
even be a dead end.
Dunno. Lotsa people get a rush outta sex on
the sneak. Continue the covert ops.
TAP-TAP. Randy stands outside, his face pressed to the window.
Heya, Ned.
They all slap on smiles, speak through gritted teeth--
(to Ned)
Heya, bait.
Found the “Free Cooking Class Coupon” you left me.
(holding up food containers)
So, I brought offal.
“Awful”?
“Offal.” O-F-F-A-L. Animal organs and
innards. For meat pies.
So, “awful.” Like this idea. I’m not leaving
Ned alone with Backroom Randy. This place is
full of freezers, perfect for body-stuffing.
It’s also full of customers. C’mon in, Randy!
Ned heads for the front door to meet Randy.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Girlies One and Two, get Frescortin’.
(as they go)
Ready? Ma.
But Calista’s PAGER has gone off. She checks it.
Dammit. My target’s on the move.
Can it wait? Thought we could have some catch-
up time while we toss that apartment.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 26.
CONTINUED: (3)
Darlin’, you know what it is to be married to
the job. There’ll be time for talking tomorrow.
She pecks his cheek. A pained Emerson can only watch her go.
But Emerson Cod couldn’t wait until tomorrow.
With each missed opportunity, the weight of the
untruths about his missing daughter grew
heavier. So heavy, that he felt he’d soon be
crushed beneath them.
Emerson rifles through papers and files in Randy’s apartment.
And so he entered the apartment of a
suspected killer with a different death on
his mind -- that of his and his mother’s
friendship. Already, he felt her pulling
away and wondered if the ever-perceptive
Calista somehow knew without knowing the
irreparable damage her son had caused.
He focuses in on an “INVOICE TO RANDY MANN” from My Best Friend,
Inc. Stamped across it: “OVERDUE: FINAL NOTICE.” Joe’s
“Frescort Profile” is clipped to it.
Tutor of some sort, my glue stick.
As Emerson Cod faced the door to the back
room, he wondered what larger lies Randy Mann
had lurking there.
Emerson draws his gun, moves to the door and throws it open.
Emerson stops in his tracks. A DARK FIGURE looms in the corner.
Freeze!
He flips on the lights. The figure is actually a TAXIDERMIED
GRIZZLY BEAR, wearing a tutu. The entire room is packed with
TAXIDERMIED ANIMALS in the VICTORIAN STYLE: mice having a tea
party, poker-playing squirrels, two frogs getting married, etc.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Holy Noah’s Nutty-as-a-fruitcake Ark.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 27.
CONTINUED:
Emerson moves to a workbench, full of taxidermy tools.
But the menagerie of taxidermied animals would
not be nuttiest thing Emerson Cod would find.
Emerson’s stunned look is on a SEALED JAR, labeled: “Joe.”
Inside, floating in clear liquid, is a human body part.
NED (PRELAP)
Yum.
Ned and Randy pull pies from the oven and put them on racks.
Meat pies. So... Sweeney.
Randy grabs a fork, dives in, but notices Ned holding back.
Aren’t you gonna chow down?
I’m a vegetarian.
Too bad. This stuff will make you strong.
“Gobbling gizzards makes muscles.” ‘Least
that’s what Mom used to say.
Um. Why?
I had loose ligaments as a kid. Always
falling, bruising my tailbone, bumping my
head. A total disaster -- especially at
sports. The kids at school always made fun,
but I didn’t care. I just played with my
pets. ‘Cause pets are cool with you, no
matter what. Like your dog. “Digby,” right?
He digs you just the way you are. Forever
will, too. Man, I gotta stop going on about
stuff like that. Makes me seem like a weirdo.
However, the Pie-Maker did not see a “weirdo.”
For he, too, knew what it was like to be an
outsider due to things outside his control. So
the Pie-Maker decided to make a connection with
the one thing at his disposal -- the truth.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 28.
CONTINUED:
I didn’t have any friends at school, either.
And you wanna talk about a disaster at sports?
They wouldn’t even give me gym clothes.
Instead, I’d sneak off on my own and bake pies.
That’s how I got started with my hobby, too.
I don’t usually share it with people, but
the minute we met, I thought you’d be okay,
so I brought it along and hid it out back.
Wanna see?
Sure.
With a flourish, Randy throws open the back door TO REVEAL: A
TAXIDERMIED DIGBY, standing on his hind legs and strumming a
guitar. And OFF Ned’s horror...
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 29.
FADE IN:
Shocked, Ned gazes at the stuffed, guitar-playing dog before
him. Randy looks on proudly.
The Pie-Maker desperately wanted to touch
Digby, for in the past, when someone he loved
died, he was able to restore their life force
with a mere tap. Only, he had already brought
Digby back once. Thus, a second stroke would
do nothing, except confirm what his eyes told
him -- his beloved companion was gone.
Listen. He’s singing “American Pie” for you.
You killed my dog!
No! That’s Butterscotch, my dog. You said
your golden retriever was staying with someone
else, so I thought I’d lend you mine. He’s
been my best friend since I was five.
This is how you repay him?
He looks happy. He makes me happy. If you
had a chance to hold onto someone you loved
after he or she died, wouldn’t you?
The Pie-Maker couldn’t tell Randy the truth:
that, yes, he would. As a matter of fact, he
had. Twice. So instead, he said:
Please leave.
I thought we might’ve had something in common.
Hurt and bewildered, Randy scoops up Butterscotch, exits, then
re-enters. Emerson Cod is behind him with a gun to his back.
You’re a sick man, Randy Mann. Stuffin’ all
those critters. Posin’ ‘em in twisted ways.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 30.
CONTINUED:
It’s why I don’t tell people about it. They
don’t understand.
Know who don’t understand? That poor hamster
you have plungin’ a toilet for all eternity.
His name is Peanut, he was my first pet and I
love him. Ned, do you think it’s twisted?
He sure does! He was just baby-sittin’ while I
gathered evidence against your murderin’ ass.
Betrayed, Randy turns to Ned, who can’t hold his gaze.
Liar. Liar.
Your pants on fire. You weren’t Joe’s
roommate. You were his client.
Why would I tell you that? It’s embarrassing,
having to pay someone to hang out with you.
Even more humiliatin’ to have your Frescort
repo’ed. Musta’ been the last straw before
you offed Joe.
No, I offered him a deal. Be my roommate,
rent-free. He agreed. Said it’d be like a
real friendship.
Is that why you kept a piece of him?
Emerson presents the jar from Randy’s apartment.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
An appendix. Floating in formaldehyde.
Which was flowing from Joe’s body. Oh, god...
‘Cept, you discovered quick that preserving a
human is tougher than a chipmunk, so you had
to dump the body instead.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 31.
CONTINUED: (2)
That appendix is mine. Joe gave it to me. As
a joke. Check his medical records. Or ask
his girlfriend. He must’ve told her about it.
What’s her name?
I don’t know. Someone at work. Guess it
was serious. Joe was even gonna quit so
they could be together.
Ned and Emerson exchange a look. OFF this:
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. MY BEST FRIEND, INC. - LOCKER ROOM - NIGHT

lines.text: Olive ties her shoe next to her locker. Chuck sidles up.
Psst. Ned just paged me at the welcome desk.
He says no doubt there’s a Downy among us.
Okay. I’ll nose around my “When Words Escape -
- How To Flatter and Reassure the Profoundly
Ugly” symposium.
And I’ve got a “Mix Discs That Matter” lab in
five. Maybe someone there will know--
BARB (O.S.)
“Kinship.” Anyone got another word for it?
I’m afraid there’s a “q” involved.
FIND Barb in the next row of lockers. She works a crossword.
“Propinquity.”
Nice! Gimme another?
Four across is “Gelding.”
Thanks, but someone else does the acrosses.
I only do the...
ANGLE ON - THE CROSSWORD - Just the downs are filled in.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 32.
CONTINUED:
...downs. Barb -- you’re Downy.
No, I’m not.
Well, you sure aren’t f-f-faking anything to
the contrary.
Barb bursts into SOBS. Chuck and Olive share a look: “Sheesh.”
We just want to help. Is Downy a nickname Joe
gave you?
Tissue... please. I’ll tell you everything...
Blubbering, Barb gestures to her open locker. Chuck and Olive
turn to it. Barb LUNGES, shoves them inside and slams the door.
BARB (CONT’D)
Fake that, bitches!
CUT TO BLACK, over which:
OLIVE (O.S.)
Crap.
Emerson unlocks his door. He stops short when, through the
glass, he sees a SILHOUETTE, rifling around in his office with a
flashlight.
Crap.
Emerson bursts in TO FIND a SKI-MASKED INTRUDER, ransacking his
filing cabinet. Emerson rushes the intruder, who vaults over
the desk in a shower of papers and office supplies.
Emerson grabs a COFFEE CUP, takes aim and drops the intruder
with a shot to the head. The figure struggles to his feet, his
hand almost to the doorknob when--
Emerson seizes him by the neck, pins him to the door. The
intruder strikes back, grabbing Emerson by the neck, as well.
Oh -- hell -- no!
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 33.
CONTINUED:
Emerson rips off the mask TO FIND -- Calista Cod. OFF this...
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 34.
FADE IN:
Emerson and Calista grip each other by the throat.
Ma?
Yes, dear?
I can’t breathe.
Yeah? I gave you breath, and this is the
thanks I get?
Calista pulls Emerson’s copy of “Lil’ GumShoe” from her satchel.
The facts were these:

scenes.heading: INT. PUBLISHING HOUSE (ONE WALL) - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: MISSY SCRIVNER sits at her desk and stamps rejection letters.
She tries to smile but can’t. Her jaw is WIRED SHUT.
Missy Scrivner, editorial assistant at Book
‘Em Books, oversaw all rejected manuscript
letters. It was a somber job, but one that
reminded her there were bigger rejects than
she. Underbite surgery had left the girl
shackled to a liquid diet, which found its way
onto the rejection letter of one Emerson Cod.
Missy’s spill smears across Emerson’s return address. She picks
up the phone, struggles MOS to get the words out.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Unable to decipher anything but the words “E”
and “Cod,” Missy phoned directory assistance.
Mistaking her garbled “E” for a “C,” the
operator gave the address of Calista, who read
the critiques of “a distant parental figure”
and “an inhumane portrayal of childhood” and
assumed her son’s secret book was:
OMIT
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 35.
BACK TO - Calista and Emerson.
A thinly-disguised tell-all! To show the
world what kind of horrible mother I was!
Did you read it?
Didn’t have to. Cover screams, “Smear
campaign!” What’s with the main character
being a girl? Ya sayin’ I turned you gay?
I ain’t gay, and this ain’t about you. It’s
about my daughter.
What daughter?
She’s seven. Her momma ran off with her when
she was a baby. Been trying to find her ever
since, with no luck. That’s why I finally
wrote “Lil’ GumShoe” -- to help her find me.
Calista opens the book. Lil’ GumShoe POPS UP, gazes at her.
Why didn’t you tell me?
I never even told my friends.
I’m not your friend. I’m your mother.
Oh, now you’re my mother.
What was that, Mumbles?
I said, only time you say that is when you
wanna make me feel guilty about somethin’.
But if you’ve switched over to Momma mode, I
can roll with that. Tell me, what kind of
mother spies on her own son?
It’s not like I wanted to.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 36.
CONTINUED:
It was an accident, huh? Know what? I think
you’re lying. Matter of fact, I bet you’re
not even on a case right now.
Calista barely flinches, but Emerson clocks it.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Damn, woman. That’s shrewd. Faked a fraud
case, set off your own beeper, even made me
take two clients at once so I’d be doubly
busy. All to poke around my personal life.
Sad thing is, I was gonna tell ya everything.
Uh-huh. After seven years of silence, you just
happened to decide to come a hundred percent
clean? What kinda fool you take me for?
Sayin’ you don’t believe me?
(off her silence)
Then there’s nothin’ left to say.
There’s a KNOCK. An agitated Ned enters.
Chuck and Olive haven’t checked in. Don’t
want to be alarmist, but what if they need--
CHUCK / OLIVE (PRELAP, O.S.)
Help!
Chuck and Olive are packed like sardines. They YELL again, then:
Why would Barb kill Joe if she was his “one
and only”?
Doesn’t matter. The fact she locked us in here
means she’s guilty of something. And if this
locker is hers, the first felony’s freesia.
“Freesia”?
Ugh. It’s like we’re trapped in a sachet in
the panty drawer of a dead shut-in, who was
shut in her bedroom by her cats so they
wouldn’t have to suffer the stench of freesia.
Can’t you smell it?
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 37.
CONTINUED:
Yes. It’s my freesia tangle-free conditioner.
Which you said smelled “amazing” yesterday.
Wish I hadn’t, now.
Wish I hadn’t, either.
Charlotte Charles and Olive Snook had been
proud of all the water flowing under their
friendship bridge. But they had been fooling
themselves, so neither was prepared for the
flash flood that was about to hit.
What?
Told you those capris make you look taller.
Liar!
No, I’m a truth-ar. I came clean unprompted.
You only admitted to lying after getting caught,
which never would’ve happened if a crazed murder
suspect hadn’t shoved us in here.
And here comes the center of the universe, pulling
us all into her gravitational orbit of blame.
FYI, there is no center of the universe
because our universe is ever expanding.
Like your neediness. “Wah, respect my feelings.”
“Wah, you can’t fence me in.” “Wah, don’t treat
me like I’m dead.” But if you’re so dead, how can
you be so needy? Oh, right. You’re selfish.
“Selfish”? I’m sharing all I own with you.
Big whoop. Secondhand stuff.
That’s what you’re angry about. The one thing
I won’t share. Ned.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 38.
CONTINUED: (2)
I cannot believe you just said that.
(off the silence)
Don’t you shrug at me in the dark, Charlotte
Charles. That was a low blow.
Well, I’m in a no-win situation. I can’t say
anything to you because it would be
insensitive. I can’t say anything to Ned
because he’s not doing anything wrong. But if
I had a nickel for every time the three of us
are together and -- unexpectedly, accidentally
-- I catch you looking at him--
Stop talking, stop talking, help-help-help!
--and you’ve got that sad, pining, “Why won’t
you love me?” look. And I start feeling like a
jerk for being in love with my own boyfriend.
A boyfriend you don’t touch.
I told you -- we can’t.
That doesn’t make sense! How can you be with
someone you can’t hold or kiss? Especially
when he’s that good a kisser.
You would know, wouldn’t you?
Yeah. I would.
I am so glad I took that bed by the window.
Petty.
Spiteful.
I’m finished!
Me, too!
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 39.
CONTINUED: (3)
At this moment, the truth-tellers had reached
the point where telling is replaced by
stomping -- off, and in opposite directions.
Fortunately, it was an urge fulfilled by the
lock-picking talents of Emerson Cod...
The door opens, revealing Emerson. Ned peers in behind him.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...who knew which lock to pick by the shouting
coming from behind it.
I’m going home. To my home.
Olive pushes her way past Ned and Emerson and exits. Chuck
steps out, tries to compose herself.
What happened?
Roommate squabble. Brought on by the
suspicious actions of Barb -- aka, Downy --
who’s definitely a person of interest.
Got an address, phone number on her?
No, but I know who would.

scenes.heading: INT. MY BEST FRIEND, INC. - BUDDY’S OFFICE - NIGHT

lines.text: The door swings open, revealing the Mod Squad.
Mr. Amicus?
ANGLE ON - THE HUG MACHINE - The BODY in it.
Shhh, Buddy’s getting a hug. We should come
back. It’s a rather religious experience.
Religious like, “Howdy, I’m God, your maker.
Come meet me.”
Emerson props up the slumped body. The Mod Squad reacts when
they see it belongs to a crushed, lifeless Barb.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 40.
CONTINUED:
Emerson turns off the machine. Ned sets his watch, touches her.
SPARK! Her eyes flutter open and land on Chuck.
Oh, good, Kitty. You got out of the locker.
Sorry ‘bout that. And I’m so sorry I called
you a bitch. That was the panic talking. I
thought you were going to tell on me.
For killing Joe?
No, for dating him. I didn’t want to get
fired. This job’s the only place...
Barb tries to continue, but can only WHEEZE.
Her lungs are crushed. Who knows CPR?
Barb raises her hand.
NED (CONT’D)
Get her to the couch.
Emerson and Chuck do so. Ned grabs a ball pump from Buddy’s bin
of sports equipment, puts the nozzle into Barb’s mouth and
inflates her.
...the only place my relentless positivity and
encyclopedic knowledge of hair braiding meant
something. I couldn’t hurt Joe. I lo--
She peters out again. As Ned gives her another PUMP--
You loved him.
When he was around, I could be my true self.
Only now, I’ll never know if it was just our
mutual passion for crosswords that brought us
together, or if he felt the same way.
He did. You were his “one and only.” He was
going to quit the company to be with you.
(holding back tears)
He said he had something important to tell me.
The night he died, I waited for his call, but he
never made it back from his Frescorting gig.
PUSHING DAISIES #204 "Frescorts" 07/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 41.
CONTINUED: (2)
Hold up. Joe wasn’t working that night.
He was moonlighting. A standing sports date.
Who with?
Joe never said, but the guy sounded tragic.
Two years of playing ball... and he was still
a spaz. Some clients simply lack the jock
gene. Buddy calls ‘em... “bleacher leechers.”
This registers with Ned.
Skip to how you ended up the main squeeze.
I was having a meltdown. Came in for a hug...
Pretended those arms were Joe’s. That’s when
the dial got turned to eleven by the Spar...
Spar... Spartan. I tried to fight--
Barb opens her hand, REVEALS a fistful of BRIGHT-RED HAIR.
You did good, Barb.
So did you. For making my sad ending... happy.
Barb smiles, and Ned re-deads her.
No Spartan’s running around killin’ popular
people. This ain’t Thermopylae High.
Right. It’s Spartanburg West...
Chuck eyes Buddy’s high school pennants, depicting the SPARTANBURG
